Outside a library in Santa Ana, California, a bronze sculpture of a dove has begun a new existence as a decentralized, participatory project. This artwork, which honors the life and legacy of Alex Odeh, was created by the Algerian-American artist Khalil Bendib in 1994. Odeh, a Palestinian-American civil rights leader and scholar, was assassinated in an October 1985 pipe bombing at his American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC) offices [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/).

## A Legacy of Resilience
Odeh’s life was shaped by early experiences of displacement and conflict. Born in Jifna, Palestine, in 1944, he lived through the 1967 occupation of the West Bank before immigrating to the United States [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/). He earned a Master’s degree in political science from California State University, Fullerton, in 1972, and eventually became a prominent director for the ADC on the West Coast, where he worked to combat anti-Arab discrimination and stereotypes [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/). Despite the gravity of his work, the investigation into his 1985 murder remains officially unsolved, with no arrests ever made for the bombing that ended his life [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/).

## The Sculpture’s Material History
The bronze dove has experienced its own series of disruptions. Over the decades, the piece has been stolen three times, splashed with red paint, and repeatedly vandalized [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/). Following recent incidents where remnants of the sculpture lay strewn about, the work underwent a shift in how it functions within the community [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/). Rather than maintaining the monument as a fixed, static object, organizers are now circulating the bronze figure through a variety of spaces [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/).

## A Living Archive
This shift toward a mobile, "living" memorial was highlighted during a 2023 residency at the Grand Central Art Center in Santa Ana, where the dove served as a focal point for performances, screenings, and conversations [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/). By removing the sculpture from its stationary pedestal, the project intends to invite new audiences into a dialogue about justice and inter-community peace—a cause Odeh himself was invested in during his lifetime [A Living Memorial to Palestinian Activist Alex Odeh Takes Flight](https://hyperallergic.com/a-living-memorial-to-palestinian-activist-alex-odeh-takes-flight/). 

The transition of the monument from a static landmark to a traveling presence offers a model for how communities might engage with historical memory. By removing the object from its original, vulnerable site, its custodians have transformed an emblem of personal loss into an ongoing conversation about the values Odeh represented. This process suggests that monuments can evolve alongside the people they are intended to serve, rather than remaining targets for the cycles of hostility that surround them.
